normalized_mechanism: Congress is constitutionally constituted as two distinct chambers: the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Representation and direct-tax apportionment operate among the States according to the population rule stated in the source text.
The number of Representatives is bounded by a maximum ratio of one Representative for every thirty thousand persons under this source rule.
Each State is guaranteed at least one Representative under the stated apportionment structure.
Before completion of the first enumeration, representation is allocated among the named States according to the source's transitional allocation.
Following the first election, Senators are procedurally divided as equally as possible into three classes.
When the President is tried by the Senate, presiding authority is assigned to the Chief Justice.
Impeachment conviction requires concurrence of two thirds of the Senate members present.
A majority of each House constitutes the quorum required to conduct business.
A number smaller than a quorum is granted the limited authority to adjourn from day to day.
Each House is granted authority to punish its own members for disorderly behavior.
Expulsion of a member by either House requires concurrence of two thirds.
Each House is required to keep a Journal of its proceedings.
Each House must publish its Journal from time to time, subject to an exception for portions it judges to require secrecy.
At the request of one fifth of members present, the yeas and nays on a question must be entered on the Journal.
During a session of Congress, either House requires consent of the other to adjourn for more than three days or to another place.
Senators and Representatives are entitled to compensation for their services, with the amount ascertained by law and payment from the United States Treasury.
Members of Congress are protected from arrest during the stated legislative attendance and travel periods, except for Treason, Felony, and Breach of the Peace.
Members may not be questioned in another place for Speech or Debate in either House.
Authority to originate bills for raising revenue is allocated to the House of Representatives.
The Senate may propose or concur with amendments to revenue bills as it may with other bills.
Votes of both Houses in the veto-reconsideration process must be determined by yeas and nays.
The names of persons voting for and against a reconsidered bill must be entered on the Journal of each House.
